questions.article: Hajj Should Inculcate Love for Humanity
questions.q: Hajj sets aside differences of race, colour and sect among the pilgrims. What does the editorial ask of the pilgrim on returning home?
options: To extend that lesson of unity to all humanity and be a well-wisher of everyone
Yes. He considers all mankind one community.
To perform the pilgrimage again each year
Not quite. The article says: To extend that lesson of unity to all humanity and be a well-wisher of everyone.
To keep to the company of fellow pilgrims
Not quite. The article says: To extend that lesson of unity to all humanity and be a well-wisher of everyone.
To avoid dealings with people of other faiths
Not quite. The article says: To extend that lesson of unity to all humanity and be a well-wisher of everyone.
questions.rationale: “This lesson of Hajj, which is aimed at inculcating unity among Muslims, should be extended to entire humanity… He has to be a well-wisher to everyone.”

questions.q: Astronomers found the light of distant galaxies shifted towards the red end of the spectrum. What did this show?
options: The galaxies are drawing closer
Not quite. The article says: The galaxies are moving away from us – the universe is expanding.
The galaxies are moving away from us – the universe is expanding
Right. Like points on a balloon as it is blown up.
The galaxies are older than was thought
Not quite. The article says: The galaxies are moving away from us – the universe is expanding.
The galaxies are cooling down
Not quite. The article says: The galaxies are moving away from us – the universe is expanding.
questions.rationale: “If all galaxies were being shifted to the red, it meant that they were all moving away from us. This meant that the universe was expanding.”

questions.q: The Prophet said the pilgrim returns as on the day his mother bore him. How does the article understand this?
options: Hajj performed in its true spirit helps a person shed his conditioning and return to his pure nature
Well read. A conscious process, not a miracle.
The pilgrim becomes physically younger
Not quite. The article says: Hajj performed in its true spirit helps a person shed his conditioning and return to his pure nature.
The pilgrim forgets his past life
Not quite. The article says: Hajj performed in its true spirit helps a person shed his conditioning and return to his pure nature.
The pilgrim need do no further good
Not quite. The article says: Hajj performed in its true spirit helps a person shed his conditioning and return to his pure nature.
questions.rationale: “Hajj is a worship which facilitates one’s de-conditioning… and brings him back to his original nature.”

questions.q: After the Farewell Sermon, the Companions set out in whatever direction their horses were facing. What lesson does the article take from this?
options: Hajj should be followed by a long rest
Not quite. The article says: The end of Hajj marks the beginning of a new task – conveying God’s message to people.
The Companions wished to leave Arabia
Not quite. The article says: The end of Hajj marks the beginning of a new task – conveying God’s message to people.
Travel is the purpose of pilgrimage
Not quite. The article says: The end of Hajj marks the beginning of a new task – conveying God’s message to people.
The end of Hajj marks the beginning of a new task – conveying God’s message to people
Yes. “Another ‘Hajj’ begins on a much vaster scale.”
questions.rationale: “This history of the Companions of the Prophet gives us the lesson that the end of Hajj marks the beginning of a new action.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, have people been given different capabilities?
options: So that cooperation becomes necessary – some lead and others support in any undertaking
Correct. Each plays the role suited to his gifts.
So that the capable may look down on others
Not quite. The article says: So that cooperation becomes necessary – some lead and others support in any undertaking.
So that people may live apart
Not quite. The article says: So that cooperation becomes necessary – some lead and others support in any undertaking.
So that only a few may succeed
Not quite. The article says: So that cooperation becomes necessary – some lead and others support in any undertaking.
questions.rationale: “There is a difference in capabilities between men, so that mutual cooperation becomes a necessity in any undertaking.”

questions.q: “I have not seen anything as desirable as Paradise whose seeker is asleep.” What does the article give as the cause of this neglect?
options: People do not believe they can succeed
Not quite. The article says: People concern themselves only with what they can see outwardly, so their minds are not awakened.
People concern themselves only with what they can see outwardly, so their minds are not awakened
Right. The greatest issue goes unconsidered.
People have been told too little
Not quite. The article says: People concern themselves only with what they can see outwardly, so their minds are not awakened.
People are too busy helping others
Not quite. The article says: People concern themselves only with what they can see outwardly, so their minds are not awakened.
questions.rationale: “This neglect is because of people’s tendency to concern themselves only with what they can see externally. As a result of this, their minds are not awakened.”

questions.q: A father rises by his own struggle, yet his children often do not match him. How does the article explain it?
options: The father kept his methods secret
Not quite. The article says: He began with discontent, which drives effort; they began with contentment, which kills motivation.
He began with discontent, which drives effort; they began with contentment, which kills motivation
Well reasoned. Deprivation can be a privilege.
The children lacked education
Not quite. The article says: He began with discontent, which drives effort; they began with contentment, which kills motivation.
Success cannot occur twice in a family
Not quite. The article says: He began with discontent, which drives effort; they began with contentment, which kills motivation.
questions.rationale: “The father started his life with the spirit of discontent, while his children started their lives with the spirit of contentment.”

questions.q: The article calls a comfort zone “a beautiful name for a non-creative zone.” What balanced advice does it give?
options: Never leave a place where you are settled
Not quite. The article says: Do not leap out of it from mere ambition, but when circumstances require change, accept it willingly.
Leave your comfort zone as often as you can
Not quite. The article says: Do not leap out of it from mere ambition, but when circumstances require change, accept it willingly.
Change only when others force you
Not quite. The article says: Do not leap out of it from mere ambition, but when circumstances require change, accept it willingly.
Do not leap out of it from mere ambition, but when circumstances require change, accept it willingly
Exactly. Change is “a circumstantial gift.”
questions.rationale: “It is not good, however, to jump out of your comfort zone simply out of ambition… But if circumstances require a change, do not be reluctant to accept it.”

questions.q: “On the Day when the truth shall be laid bare…” (68:42). What does the article say will then count?
options: Skill in speaking
Not quite. The article says: Sincerity, truthfulness and effort made to please God – not show, wealth or fame.
The respect one enjoyed in the world
Not quite. The article says: Sincerity, truthfulness and effort made to please God – not show, wealth or fame.
Sincerity, truthfulness and effort made to please God – not show, wealth or fame
Yes. Pretence cannot pass there.
The number of one’s supporters
Not quite. The article says: Sincerity, truthfulness and effort made to please God – not show, wealth or fame.
questions.rationale: “On the Day of Judgment, only that person will be held deserving of rewards who had made effort in this world to please God.”

questions.q: Why does the article contrast a “family prescription” with a scientifically prepared medicine?
options: To show that old medicines were always harmful
Not quite. The article says: To show that the modern mind accepts only what is supported by evidence open to testing, so ideas must be presented that way.
To praise family traditions
Not quite. The article says: To show that the modern mind accepts only what is supported by evidence open to testing, so ideas must be presented that way.
To show that the modern mind accepts only what is supported by evidence open to testing, so ideas must be presented that way
Well read. Long usage alone no longer persuades.
To warn against trusting doctors
Not quite. The article says: To show that the modern mind accepts only what is supported by evidence open to testing, so ideas must be presented that way.
questions.rationale: “Today’s customer seeks that product which has been manufactured on scientific lines. Likewise it is only those ideas whose truth is verified by natural realities that he is ready to accept.”
